name: ridgeline-query-manifest-v2
purpose: Assigns every benchmark query a capability class and a metric tier so that retrieval is scored only on what retrieval can produce. No query wording was altered; labels changed, queries did not.

tier_definitions.T1: finding-level retrieval — a passage or row states the conclusion; retrieval recall is valid
tier_definitions.T2: operand retrieval — retrieval must surface sources; the conclusion needs another component
tier_definitions.T3: retrieval invalid — no chunk can satisfy the task; any retrieval metric is an invented number

not_scored_T3.reason: source document has zero chunks; unretrievable by construction

superseded_metric.why_wrong: counted all 19 R1 findings as retrieval tasks, including RDG-021 whose source has zero chunks, and reported operand retrieval as finding recall
superseded_metric.replacement: T1 retrieval recall and T2 operand recall, reported separately

metrics_r1.miss_cause_note: A miss is not always a retrieval failure. RDG-009's source documents rank 1 and 2 with the abstention gate disabled — retrieval succeeded and the gate discarded the result. RDG-015 is never retrieved at depth 500 and is a genuine ranking miss. RDG-008 ranks 15, just outside the window. Reporting all three as 'retrieval misses' hides three different causes with three different owners.

small_sample_warning: T1 has 2 eligible queries. No rate computed over it is statistically meaningful — the Wilson 95% interval on 1/2 spans roughly 3%-97%. It is reported to be honest about how little finding-level retrieval this fixture actually tests, not as a performance claim.
